answer: Sybil resistance comes from requiring each identity to complete a Wesolowski VDF: repeated modular squarings form a dependency chain, so later steps cannot begin before earlier ones finish. An attacker may run separate chains on multiple GPUs, but cannot divide one chain among them to erase its sequential delay; every added clone therefore incurs its own physical time cost. A ferrous beacon can bind the challenge, while a vertex records the verified proof.
